html:
Chud was the name the early East Slavic chronicles gave to Baltic Finnic peoples, above all the ancestors of the Estonians. On the map for 900 and 1000 the Chuds hold today's Estonia.

The Primary Chronicle lists the Chud with the Slovenes and Krivichs among the peoples who invited Rurik to rule. Rus princes later tried to make them pay tribute: in 1030 Yaroslav the Wise founded a fort called Yuryev, today's Tartu, in their land. Lake Peipus is still called Lake Chud in Russian, and the Battle on the Ice of 1242 was fought on it. See also Ests and Veps.
sum: Chud was the name the early East Slavic chronicles gave to Baltic Finnic peoples, above all the ancestors of the Estonians. On the map for 900 and 1000 the Chuds hold today's Estonia.
